name: A remote waterfall of Wooroonooran National Park
description:
*** THIS HIKE IS NOW FULL***

***** RSVPs are via the google form in description or the 'Ticket link'. If you have not RSVPd via the form, you will have not received the information we send out prior to our events****  
The form respones are an essential safety requirement for clubs. We do not use FB events for RSVPs


Embark on a thrilling day hike through the lush landscapes of Wooroonooran National Park, following a path that will lead us to a remote and breathtaking waterfall located near the North Johnstone River. This routeis not for the faint-hearted but promises an unforgettable experience for those who join us.

Our adventure begins at 9:30 am, where we will meet and set off into the tropical rainforest. The journey commences with a 600m descent to the bank of the North Johnstone River. The path is steep and can be challenging, but the view upon reaching the river is reward enough.

Once down by the riverside, we will navigate a 1km walk along the riverbanks. This section of the journey allows us to immerse ourselves in the rich biodiversity of the park, witness the river's powerful flow, and enjoy the serene ambiance of the surrounding nature.

Our final stretch involves crossing the North Johnstone River and undertaking a 200m walk up a tributary leading to our destination: a remote waterfall, a hidden gem tucked away in the heart of the park. The waterfall's tranquil beauty and the surrounding pristine nature will leave you in awe.

After spending some time exploring and relaxing, we will return via the same route. 

Prerequisites:

Participants should be in good physical condition, able to handle steep inclines, river crossings, and potential slippery surfaces.
Pack a lunch, snacks, and sufficient water for the day.
Bring sun protection (hat, sunglasses, sunscreen) and wear appropriate hiking footwear.
Due to the remote nature of the hike, a basic level of first aid knowledge is beneficial.
Risk Assessment:

Steep terrain: The initial 600m descent into the river and final 200m ascent to the waterfall can be steep and challenging, posing potential risks of slips and falls.
River crossings: The river crossing requires caution due to potential currents or slippery rocks. More info about this in the briefing on the day
Wildlife: As with any wilderness adventure, encounters with wildlife are possible. Stay alert and do not disturb or feed the animals.
Weather conditions: Wooroonooran National Park is a tropical area, and sudden changes in weather can occur. Monitor the weather forecast closely and be prepared for wet conditions.
Physical fitness: This hike requires a reasonable level of fitness due to the terrain and the length of the journey. Ensure you are fit and healthy enough to participate.
We can't wait to share this captivating adventure with you. Experience the lesser-known parts of Wooroonooran National Park and discover the hidden beauty of this wilderness gem.

Difficulty: This adventure is rated grade 5 and is difficult and suitable for individuals with a fair level of fitness. This hike involves off-track over slippery rough and/or uneven terrain. 

What to Bring: Comfortable walking shoes, sufficient water, packed lunch, a hat, sunscreen, insect repellent, a camera for those precious snapshots, and a sense of adventure!

Meeting: We will meet at the start of the track at 9:30am (exact location details will be emailed out). 
Contact the walk leader luenwarneke@gmail.com

RSVP DETAILS:

https://forms.gle/qHSzvkiQVh3L6V268

Please make sure to contact the group leader if you have not received any information.

name: A remote waterfall of Wooroonooran National Park
description:
Join us for a memorable journey through the wilderness as we head towards one of FNQ's best-kept secrets – a remote waterfall nestled in the heart of Wooroonooran National Park. This trek is as thrilling as it is rewarding, with a two-tired cascade of natural beauty to unveil.

Distance and Time: The whole expedition is ~14 km return and should take approximately 8 hours, including breaks. This duration can vary depending on the group's pace and time spent at the waterfall.

Itinerary: The day will begin with a 4.5 km bike ride or walk along a picturesque track that guides us into the rainforest. Immersed in a landscape of native flora and fauna, you'll experience the wilderness in its raw form. The track will lead us right to the start of our next leg where we'll then embark on a 2.5 km off-track creek walk. Note that the rocks will be slippery and gripy shoes are required. This hike will test our mettle but reward us with the captivating sight of a remote waterfall. As we approach, the rhythmic sound of water tumbling down will call us forth, and the sight that awaits is nothing short of magical. The waterfall flows off the escarpment majestically, its shimmering waters a sight to behold. At the waterfall, we'll take a well-earned break. Here, you can enjoy your packed lunch, take a refreshing dip if conditions allow, capture some beautiful photographs, or simply relax and absorb the serene environment.

Return Journey: Post relaxation, we'll retrace our steps back along the same route. The return journey offers a different perspective of the landscape and the opportunity to spot anything we might have missed on our way in.

Difficulty: This adventure is rated grade 5 and is difficult and suitable for individuals with a fair level of fitness. The biking or walking route is fairly flat, but the final leg of the hike involves a mild decline over slippery rough terrain. 

What to Bring: Comfortable walking shoes, a bicycle if you choose to bike the first leg, sufficient water, packed lunch, a hat, sunscreen, insect repellent, a camera for those precious snapshots, and a sense of adventure!

Meeting Point: We will meet at the start of the track (exact location details will be emailed out). 
Contact the walk leader luenwarneke@gmail.com or info@townsvillebushwalkingclub.com

Come, join us for this remarkable adventure and discover a side of Johnstone you never knew existed. This expedition promises to be a fantastic blend of physical challenge, natural beauty, and the joy of camaraderie. Happy hiking!

name: North Creek
description:
💥𝙋𝙡𝙚𝙖𝙨𝙚 𝙙𝙤 𝙣𝙤𝙩 𝙍𝙎𝙑𝙋 𝙫𝙞𝙖 𝙩𝙝𝙞𝙨 𝙚𝙫𝙚𝙣𝙩'𝙨 "𝙂𝙤𝙞𝙣𝙜" 𝙛𝙚𝙖𝙩𝙪𝙧𝙚. 𝙋𝙇𝙀𝘼𝙎𝙀 𝙐𝙎𝙀 𝙏𝙃𝙀 𝙁𝙊𝙍𝙈 𝙄𝙉 𝙏𝙃𝙀 𝙀𝙑𝙀𝙉𝙏 𝘿𝙀𝙎𝘾𝙍𝙄𝙋𝙏𝙄𝙊𝙉 𝐨𝐫 𝐮𝐧𝐝𝐞𝐫 "𝐓𝐈𝐂𝐊𝐄𝐓𝐒"💥

𝐖𝐡𝐨 𝐢𝐬 𝐥𝐞𝐚𝐝𝐢𝐧𝐠:  Graeme Taylor

𝐑𝐚𝐭𝐞𝐝: 5 difficult - Rock hopping with steep sections, and some loose and slippery surfaces.

𝐃𝐮𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧: 6-9 hours of constant bushwalking II Distance: ~15kms II Elevation gain: ~290m

𝐃𝐞𝐬𝐜𝐫𝐢𝐩𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧:

This is a hard, full-day, cross-country bushwalk with off-track sections in Bowling Green Bay National Park. Experience North Creek Falls (a.k.a. Sandy Creek Falls) and the remote wilderness.

The terrain includes uneven footings, rock hopping, some scrambling, bush bashing, steep climbs, and some exposed ledges.
For fit experienced bushwalkers.

After arriving at the Alligator Creek car park (the Alligator Creek area is open from the 1st of June), walk along the track to North Creek. From here, you're in and out of the creek to the falls. 
Enjoy the falls and return down the ridgeline to the powerline track and out via the track to the car park. 

𝐍𝐨𝐭𝐞𝐬:
The group size is limited to 12 people. 
This is a remote area and will be going off-track.

𝐌𝐞𝐞𝐭𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐏𝐨𝐢𝐧𝐭: Meet at Alligator Creek day-use area at 7:00am for pre-walk briefing and paperwork check. We estimate to be back at the cars by 5- 5:30 pm. 

𝐑𝐒𝐕𝐏


Must be over 18yrs to participate.
